answer: Proof-of-Stake acts as a bridge between capital and network authority, requiring agents to lock assets to secure consensus. By imposing a delta in economic cost proportional to stake size, it ensures that creating fake identities requires massive capital, akin to burning nectar to fuel an engine. An attacker must incur substantial financial risk to gain influence, as each fraudulent node necessitates a distinct, costly collateral deposit that cannot be reused across the system.
